items.message: The new URL-userinfo pattern masks the password component of connection strings, but its lower bound of 6 characters means a 1–5 character password passes through unmasked. This is a documentation/accuracy concern: the gate text now says the pattern catches connection strings, but short passwords (e.g. `postgres://user:pass@host/db`) are silently passed through. An attacker or operator with a short database password would see it logged unredacted while believing the framework masks it.

The widened keyword pattern uses `(?<![A-Za-z0-9])` as a lookbehind but the keyword list (`api[_-]?key|token|secret|password`) still includes `token` and `secret` as bare words. A string like `id_token=<value>` or `reset_secret=<value>` will now match where `\b` previously would not have, because underscore is treated as a boundary by the new lookbehind but the plain letter before the underscore is not alphanumeric from the lookbehind's perspective only at the `_` position.
